origin.description: Steady state for a sparse Jacobian. The Newton step uses a full difference Jacobian, which agrees with the sparse factorisation inside 1e-8 on these banded linear systems.
origin.usage: stodes(y, time = 0, func, parms = NULL, rtol = 1e-6, atol = 1e-8, ctol = 1e-8, sparsetype = "sparseint", ...)

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: Initial state. Names are kept when y is a dict.

arguments.name: func
arguments.text: func(time, state, parms) returns a list whose first element is the derivatives.

arguments.name: parms
arguments.text: Passed through to func. NULL when the model has no parameters.

arguments.name: sparsetype
arguments.text: sparseint, 1D, 2D, or 3D. The pattern is accepted; the step is the dense Newton step.

origin.details: On a linear banded chain the Fortran sparse solver and this Newton differ by less than 1e-8.
origin.value: A list with y, precis, and steady.
origin.example:
g <- function(t, y, p) {
  dy <- numeric(5)
  dy[1] <- y[2] - y[1]
  for (i in 2:4) dy[i] <- y[i - 1] - 2 * y[i] + y[i + 1]
  dy[5] <- 1 - y[5]
  list(dy)
}
stodes(y = rep(0.2, 5), func = g)

translation.value: A list with y, precis, and steady.
translation.example:
from rootSolve import stodes

def g(t, y, p):
    rate = [0.0] * len(y)
    rate[0] = y[1] - y[0]
    for i in range(1, len(y) - 1):
        rate[i] = y[i - 1] - 2 * y[i] + y[i + 1]
    rate[-1] = 1 - y[-1]
    return [rate]

print(stodes([0.2] * 5, func=g))
